extracted.intended_audience: actors, theatre critics, theatrical historians, and informed general readers interested in performance evaluation
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted criteria for judging a tragic actor's stage performance (voice, physicality, interpretation, presence, etc.), as exemplified by contemporary 19th-century London newspaper reviews of Edwin Forrest. Useful for acting criticism, casting, or performance study.

rubrics_metrics.name: Naturalness vs. stage chant
rubrics_metrics.description: Declamation should be 'perfectly free from the usual stage chant, catchings, and points' and modeled on nature rather than artificial mannerisms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid mechanistic, sing-song delivery and stage 'points'; aim for speech that 'fell like music' and appears natural. Anti-pattern: over-declamatory, theatrical chant that calls attention to itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Physical presence and figure
rubrics_metrics.description: A commanding physical presence, often described in terms like 'graceful and symmetrical person,' 'more than the ordinary stature,' or 'figure a model for stage effect,' contributes to effectiveness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stage physique should suit the role (e.g., Spartacus benefits from a muscular, heroic physique). Note caveat: qualities that suit one part may 'unfit him for those loftier conceptions'—physical type must match character demands.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voice quality and power
rubrics_metrics.description: Voice described as 'rich and deep,' 'replete with a rough music,' 'voice of deep and earnest power' and capable of tenderness and transitions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Voice should have tonal variety, power for projection, and the capacity for tender undertones. Antipatterns: monotone, weak projection, or affected patois/enunciation problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enunciation and diction
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear enunciation 'to the last recorded syllable' is praised; speech should be intelligible and musical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Precise diction helps the audience follow both declamatory and quiet passages. Example praise: enunciation falling 'like music on the ears.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Emotional sincerity and authenticity
rubrics_metrics.description: Passion and pathos must seem sincere and unsophisticated—'his pathos is equally sincere and unsophisticated'—not mere tricks of the stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emotion should feel rooted in character rather than be theatrical posturing. Anti-pattern: affectation, exaggerated grimace, or pantomimic sentimentality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control and self-command
rubrics_metrics.description: Even in violent passion the actor should retain 'self-control'—be 'the master, not the slave, of his feelings'—never extravagant merely for show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Balance strong feeling with judgment and restraint; avoid uncontrolled ranting or over-extravagance. Praised when passion is 'from the heart, and never from the lungs.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment and discrimination in interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Acting displays 'great tact, discrimination, and effect' and 'studied the character with the judgment of a scholar.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose which moments to intensify or subdue; interpret character with informed choices rather than surface mannerisms. Example: selecting striking situations and giving them measured emphasis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistency and coherence across the role
rubrics_metrics.description: Each scene should be 'in strict keeping with those that had preceded it,' giving 'a consistent transcript of the whole matter' and 'embodied... strict identity with the person represented.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain psychological and physical continuity across acts so the portrayal reads as one coherent character. Anti-pattern: disjointed or uneven characterization from scene to scene.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness of style to the role
rubrics_metrics.description: The actor's style must suit the character: e.g., 'gave a sense of dignified and quiet power' instead of the fashionable 'rant.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt dignity, colloquialism, or grandeur according to the role; avoid mannerisms incongruent with the character's nature. Example fault: using drawling/measured delivery where colloquial familiarity is needed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Variety and modulation of action
rubrics_metrics.description: Action should be 'easy, graceful, and varied' and 'bold, unconscious, and diversified' rather than monotonous.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physical movement and gesture should change appropriately with emotional shifts; avoid repetitive or mechanical gestures that reduce interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facial expressiveness and feature suitability
rubrics_metrics.description: A face 'capable of the sternest as of the nicest delineations of passion' is prized, though critics note some actors' features 'not capable of much variety.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use facial expression to convey subtle shifts; if physiognomy limits variety, compensate with voice and movement. Antipattern: relying solely on exaggerated facial contortions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and avoidance of copyism
rubrics_metrics.description: Performance should not be an imitation ('not the manner of a copyist') but offer new readings that convey 'new ideas.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bring individual conceptions to familiar roles; novel readings that cohere with the character are praised. Anti-pattern: slavish mimicry of celebrated predecessors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depth of conception and imaginative apprehension
rubrics_metrics.description: Excellent performances 'sound its depths' and show 'elevation of thought and sentiment'—an imaginative, learned apprehension of character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Aim for an interpretation that reveals psychological and thematic layers of the role, not just surface action. Example: seeing Othello as a 'high-toned, chivalrous Moor' rather than only a fiery warrior.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriateness and restraint in physical energy
rubrics_metrics.description: Bursts of physical energy should be 'overwhelming' when needed but 'without 'o'erstepping the modesty of nature''; strength must not become grotesque.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use athleticism and force where character demands—but within natural limits so it remains believable. Anti-pattern: excessive muscular display that sacrifices aesthetic proportion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ability to carry the piece / sustain a leading role
rubrics_metrics.description: When 'the whole weight of the piece rests upon him alone,' the actor must 'nobly sustain it' and be capable of exhausting but sustained performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Endurance—emotional and physical—and capacity to maintain quality throughout a lengthy or demanding role are required. Example praise: sustaining performance 'to the close with undiminished power.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Taste in costume and bearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Dressing 'with taste and magnificence' and carrying oneself with 'grace and dignity' contribute to the stage picture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Costume and bearing should support the interpretation without distracting; polish in external presentation complements internal work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of transitions and pacing
rubrics_metrics.description: Transitions of feeling should be 'finely marked' and vocal transitions used judiciously; one critic noted he employed transitions 'somewhat too frequently.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Manage pacing so the shifts in emotion feel organic; avoid overusing dramatic vocal or physical changes that call attention to technique rather than character.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realism in specific scenes (scene truth)
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual scenes (e.g., a drunken brawl or bedchamber scene) should be convincing and realistic—'strikingly impressive of reality.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work to make each episode believable in its circumstances; scene-level realism enhances overall credibility. Anti-pattern: theatrical caricature in intimate or violent scenes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality / accessibility to broad audiences
rubrics_metrics.description: An actor should appeal beyond a 'fastidious coterie'—giving 'free play to those rough natural passions which are intelligible all the world over.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Favor clarity and elemental emotional truth that can move general audiences while retaining artistic integrity. Antipattern: performances tailored only to elite tastes that alienate general spectators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoidance of theatrical tricks and affectation
rubrics_metrics.description: Superior acting is noted for absence of 'stage-trick and undue gesticulation' and for not relying on 'pretty tinkling poetic passage' delivery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not use gimmicks to elicit applause; let character truth produce effect. Examples of anti-patterns: stage trickery, gratuitous gesticulation, and melodramatic flourishes.
